newsitem.title: USA: Court rejects union bid to keep ValuJet grounded.
newsitem.headline: Court rejects union bid to keep ValuJet grounded.

text.p: A U.S. court of appeals has rejected a union request to keep ValuJet Airlines grounded pending an appeal to the carrier's Transportation Department's recertification, the union said on Monday.
But the Association of Flight Attendants said it would continue to press its appeal to overturn the department action announced last Thursday.
ValuJet was to resume flights later Monday.

The airline was grounded on June 17 after an intense safety inspection following a crash on May 11 in Florida showed a series off unsafe maintenance practices, since corrected, the Federal Aviation Administration said.

"We are disappointed that the stay was not granted," said David Borer, general counsel for the flight attendants' union. "The DOT decision is a bad precedent. We intend to pursue the appeal in order to force the DOT to follow its own regulations and uphold the highest standards of airline safety."
